# How to succeed in this course {#how-to-succeed .unnumbered}

Success in QM is not about talent for mathematics. It is about a short
weekly routine that you repeat: **prepare before class, take part in class,
read and practise after class, and bring your attempts to the tutorial.**
Every lecture chapter follows this routine.

Why this routine works:

- If you prepare, the lecture is your second look at each idea, not your
  first. You can then use the lecture for questions and examples.
- The lecture covers the main ideas of each chapter and leaves room for
  questions and for trying tasks yourself. The chapter has the full material, with every
  step, example, and piece of code. This is why the first step after class
  is to read the lecture material once in full.
- Answering a few recall questions on the same day helps you remember the
  material. On that day, this costs you the least time.
- Each chapter has review questions on earlier lectures, because each
  lecture builds on the earlier ones.
- The tutorials prepare you for the exam only if you arrive with your own
  attempts. Wrong attempts are the most useful ones.

Practice spread over the weeks works better than the same amount of work
packed together before the exam.

## What is examined

The lecture material and the tutorials are the exam material. Grey
**Optional** boxes are not exam material. They contain formal versions, derivations, and extra topics for
students who are interested.

## In the lecture

In the lecture you often try a question with your neighbour before the
answer is shown. Try it seriously, even when the question looks hard. A wrong
attempt helps you learn. In QM Intermediate, bring your laptop. The code of
the lecture is in the chapter, ready to copy. You can run each step yourself
and get the same numbers and figures.

## The calendar at a glance

Both courses run from 19 October to 3 December 2026 (weeks 43 to 49). You find
the rooms in your personal timetable. If a time in your timetable differs from
this page, follow the timetable.

**QM Basic (year 1):** lectures on Monday at 14:45 and on Thursday at 10:45.
Tutorials 1 to 3 follow Lectures 3, 6, and 9, and Tutorial 4 follows
Lecture 10. Tutorial 2 covers Lectures 4 and 5. Tutorials are on Thursday at
10:45 or at 12:45, depending on your group. One exception: Lecture 3 on
Monday 26 October starts at 10:45.

**Exams.** Both courses end with one exam that counts for 100% of the grade.
All exam questions are open questions. The QM Basic exam is a closed-book
written exam of 180 minutes, with the formula sheet attached. You may use a
calculator of the Casio FX-82 series or of the Texas Instruments TI-30 series,
but not the TI-30X Pro. You take the QM
Intermediate exam in TestVision, and it lasts 120 minutes. You may use RStudio,
Excel, the TestVision calculator, a simple pocket calculator, scrap paper,
and the code sheet.

Each exam has 100 points. Your test score is the number of points divided
by 10, with two decimals and a minimum of 1.00. The lecturer enters this score
in Osiris, and Osiris rounds it to a whole or half grade for your final course
grade. A score from 5.50 to 5.74 becomes 6.0, and a score from 5.25 to 5.49
becomes 5.0. For example, 72 points give a test score of 7.20 and a final
grade of 7.0. You pass with a final grade of 6.0 or higher, that is with 55
points or more.

| Course | Exam | Resit |
|---|---|---|
| QM Basic | Tuesday 8 December 2026 | Monday 18 January 2027 |
| QM Intermediate | Thursday 17 December 2026 | Thursday 21 January 2027 |

The dates come from Osiris and can change. The time and the room are in your
exam schedule. Each course has a mock exam with model answers in this book:
the [QM Basic Mock Exam](../basic/mock-exam.qmd) and the
[QM Intermediate Mock Exam](../intermediate/mock-exam.qmd).

## Printable weekly checklists

The course period has four types of week. Print this page or copy the
relevant list into your planner at the start of each week.

### QM Basic: week with two lectures (weeks 43, 45, 47)

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Two-lecture week

- <span class="day">Friday before</span> (free morning): preparation
  videos for Monday's lecture, preparation task, prediction
- <span class="day">Monday</span>: 14:45 lecture · evening: read the
  lecture material, answer the recall questions
- <span class="day">Tuesday</span> (free day): practice tasks for
  Monday's lecture · review questions from earlier lectures
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span> (around your one EiA session):
  preparation videos for Thursday's lecture, preparation task, prediction
- <span class="day">Thursday</span>: 10:45 lecture · afternoon: read
  the lecture material, answer the recall questions
- <span class="day">Friday</span>: practice tasks for Thursday's
  lecture · "Make it yours", two sentences · prepare for Monday
:::

### QM Basic: week with one lecture and a tutorial (weeks 44, 46, 48, 49)

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Lecture-plus-tutorial week

- <span class="day">Friday before</span>: preparation for Monday's lecture
- <span class="day">Monday</span>: lecture (14:45, in week 44 at 10:45) · read the lecture
  material, answer the recall questions
- <span class="day">Tuesday</span>: practice tasks for Monday's
  lecture
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span>: attempt the tutorial tasks
  yourself first (AI allowed, following the protocol below), mark where you
  got stuck
- <span class="day">Thursday</span>: tutorial at 10:45 or 12:45 (exam preparation session),
  bring your attempts · redo the task you could not solve
- <span class="day">Friday</span>: finish the tutorial set
  on your own · extra exercises with worked solutions from
  the Tilly bot of your course · "Make it yours" · prepare for Monday
:::

### QM Intermediate: standard week (one Wednesday lecture)

In QM Intermediate you do one round of work per week, spread over several
days.

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Standard week

- <span class="day">Monday or Tuesday</span> (before the
  lecture): preparation video, preparation question, R warm-up, bring the
  output
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span>: QM lecture (the start time changes,
  see the table above), bring your laptop · evening: read the lecture material,
  answer the recall questions
- <span class="day">Thursday or Friday</span> (around your EiA3
  slot): the practice tasks after class · one review question from an
  earlier lecture · "Make it yours", two sentences about your EiA3 venture
:::

### QM Intermediate: tutorial week (weeks 45 and 48)

The tutorial is on the day after the lecture, so you cannot wait until the
end of the week with your attempts. The tutorial covers the three lectures
before it. The tutorial page
says which lecture each task uses. Start with the tasks on the two earlier lectures.

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Tutorial week

- <span class="day">Monday or Tuesday</span>: preparation for Wednesday's
  lecture · attempt the tutorial tasks that use the earlier
  lectures, AI allowed following the protocol below, mark where you got
  stuck
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span>: QM lecture · evening: read the
  lecture material · attempt the tutorial tasks that use today's
  lecture
- <span class="day">Thursday</span>: tutorial (exam preparation session), bring
  your attempts and the points where you got stuck
- <span class="day">Friday or weekend</span>: redo the tasks
  that you got wrong in the tutorial, on your own · the recall questions and practice
  tasks of Wednesday's lecture · "Make it yours"
:::

## Working with AI, in one paragraph

Use the Tilly bot of your course (linked on the course overview page)
and other AI tools with the
protocol **Attempt → Ask → Verify → Explain**. Attempt the task
yourself first and find where you are stuck. Ask for a hint or for a question
that helps you find your mistake, not for a full solution. Verify every answer against the data, the
course notation, and the R output. Then explain the result in your own
words. What counts in this course is what you can do yourself with data and
output. With this protocol, AI improves this skill instead of replacing it.

## If you fall behind

Do not try to catch up by reading everything you missed. Go to the chapter of
the most recent lecture. Read its lecture material once, answer its recall
questions, and do its first practice task. Bring what you cannot solve to the
next tutorial or to Tilly. One finished round on the current lecture is worth
more than reading three older chapters without practising. The
[Mathematics Refresher](math-refresher.qmd) and
[R Refresher](r-refresher.qmd) are there so that something you missed in an
earlier course never stops you in this one.

[Continue to the R Refresher](r-refresher.qmd).
